title: Plantation revues and acts: Ada Brown
summary: Dancers, blues singer Ada Brown and the changing revue format at the Plantation.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Do you remember Half Plane Jackson, Frankie Jackson? Singer and entertainer, you know?
I think your name is familiar. Maybe I do. A little short, then. Half Plane, I think I remember. It's a long time ago.
I just wondered who was in those reviews.

Now the names got away from...let's see. Oh yeah, Dickie Wells and Jimmy and Dickie, they were two dancers. They were young. And who else? You had a girl, she came to New York later on. She was a very good singer and dancer, although she used to do a split, and split all across the slope. I've forgotten her name. She was gonna sing a little bit. And who else? Oh. There was a blues singer, a big one like...she was from St. Louis, Missouri. She had a hell of a voice, a big sound like the first blues singer. What's her name? The first one.
When I think of Ma Rainey and Bessie Smith.
Bessie Smith. She was like Bessie. She was big like Bessie. And she had the same sound. She sang some beautiful blues also. Around 24 and 25. Forget her name. So you had lots of acts along with them.

You had a review of what, ten girls dancing. And you had individual artists like singers and tap dancers. You know, things like that. Bill Robinson's dancing now playing songs. You had tumblers. An act that used to tumble. And every two weeks they changed the show. Then another show. But you keep the same chorus. But new stars would come in every week. That was Ada Brown, I think. Ada Brown, that's her. That's her.
No, no. That's the one I'm referring to. Yeah. She was at the plantation. Yeah, that's that. Ada Brown, that's her name.
I think she was James Scott's cousin. You know the guy that wrote Climax Rag and all that.
What? Yeah, but I know she was a big one. She had a sound. She could sing. Ada Brown, that's her. I think she did, man.
She made Panama Limited and all that. She had a sound, man.
We used to push that guy. Oh, yeah. Tell you the problem.
